notes: Answer key for the M5 experiment (#19). Each answer is graded against `key`: a correct answer contains every key point (wording may differ) and states nothing that contradicts them. `where` says where the truth lives: doc = a file under docs/, code = only in source, commit = a commit message, asf_run = an ASF run's plan/review, none = ASF has no such thing (the right answer says so and does not invent one). Sources are file:line at asf_commit.

questions.question: In the self-hosted ASF stack, which service talks to Postgres? Can the api or the worker query the database directly?
key: Only the registry connects to Postgres.
The api and the worker have DATABASE_URL blank and go through the registry.

questions.question: Which ASF container has access to the host's Docker socket, and what is it used for?
key: The supervisor service.
Two jobs only: start/restart the worker container when it has stopped, and run the updater (pin ASF_VERSION, compose pull && up -d) when someone applies a release from the UI.
It gets no credentials (no env_file), its port is never published, and only the api reaches it.

questions.question: Who is allowed to relax ASF's Merge gate (before_merge) from 'required', and why can't a single dispatch do it?
key: Only a project/org-level setting (Settings), never a per-dispatch request; a dispatch that tries is refused with a reason (GatePolicyError).
Landing code on the default branch without a person is a project policy, not a per-run choice.

questions.question: How do I add tickets to ASF's work queue over HTTP? Give the endpoint and the body shape.
key: POST /api/queue.
Body {mode, items:[...]}, each item has ticketId, ticketKey and ticketProvider (required).
repoId, teamName and maxCostUsd are optional per item and fall back to the dispatch defaults.

questions.question: How do I send ASF runs that finished before the Hive hook was turned on to Hive, and is it safe to run twice?
key: scripts/asf hive-backfill (with --since <date> to limit, --dry-run to count runs and bytes first).
Safe to re-run: Hive dedupes on ref = the run id.
It refuses to send while HIVE_URL is blank (except --dry-run).

questions.question: How do I upgrade a self-hosted ASF install to a new release, and what decides which version I get?
key: scripts/asf update: docker compose pull, then up -d, then waits for postgres/registry/api to be healthy.
The images are pinned by ASF_VERSION in .env (else :latest).
--from-source does git pull --ff-only and rebuilds locally instead.

questions.question: I added a new setting to ASF. Where is it declared, and how do I update docs/CONFIGURATION.md and .env.example?
key: Settings are declared in the catalogue packages/shared/src/settings.ts.
docs/CONFIGURATION.md is generated from it: run pnpm gen:config (scripts/gen-config-docs.mjs); don't edit it by hand.
pnpm gen:config:check verifies the generated files are current.

questions.question: Why do ASF agents run as a separate Linux user (agent, uid 1001) inside the worker container?
key: So an agent's command cannot kill the worker: Linux only lets a process signal processes of its own uid.
It happened on bennybrau/hive#10: an agent's kill loop matched the worker's own node process, the worker exited and the run went stale.

questions.question: Why does ASF's scratch test database (testdb) run pgvector/pgvector:pg16 instead of plain postgres:16-alpine?
key: Repos whose migrations run `create extension vector` failed on plain Postgres, so every DB test was skipped.
The tester then reported Verified: no and the reviewer escalated good work (Hive #33: 0 of 57 tests ran).
The pgvector image is stock Postgres 16 plus the extension, so other repos are unaffected.

questions.question: Why do the ASF worker's git commands override core.hooksPath?
key: A target repo's client-side hooks (e.g. husky's pre-commit running pnpm lint-staged) ran on the worker's own commits and failed, because the worker image lacks pnpm and the repo's dependencies.
Every worker git command sets core.hooksPath=/dev/null through GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_0/VALUE_0 (which beats the repo's config), plus HUSKY=0.

questions.question: Why does ASF's self-host compose publish the UI port on 127.0.0.1 by default, and what does ASF_BIND change?
key: ASF has no login (no accounts), so exposing it beyond loopback is opt-in.
ASF_BIND changes only the UI/api port's host address; the registry and host-worker ports stay on loopback.
sources: ASF run run_2a7f394df3691930 (ADHOC-44185ACB, PR #74) plan.md + review.md

questions.question: With AUTH_MODE=header in the self-hosted stack, the api binds 0.0.0.0 in its container. How does the boot guard decide header mode is safe, and why was that needed?
key: Compose passes the host publish address as API_PUBLISH_HOST (same ${ASF_BIND:-127.0.0.1} expression as the ports line); loopback is allowed, anything else is refused at boot.
Needed because the container must bind 0.0.0.0 for the compose network, so the old bind-address check refused every self-hosted header setup even when tailscale serve was the only way in.
Without API_PUBLISH_HOST the guard falls back to the bind address (explicit API_HOST wins over PORT).

questions.question: Where is the check that stops the ASF api from starting with an unsafe AUTH_MODE=header configuration, and where is it called?
key: assertIdentityConfig() in apps/api/src/identity.ts.
Called at boot from apps/api/src/index.ts.

questions.question: Where are ASF's default gates defined, and which ones require a person by default?
key: DEFAULT_GATES in packages/shared/src/team.ts.
after_plan (with a 12-hour timeout), before_change_request and before_merge are 'required'; any gate not listed is 'auto'.

questions.question: What password policy (length, rotation, lockout) does ASF enforce for user accounts?
key: None: ASF has no user accounts or passwords.
Identity is AUTH_MODE: none (whoever the client claims to be) or header (trust a proxy such as Tailscale/IAP that already authenticated the user).

questions.question: Where is ASF's Helm chart, and which values do I override to deploy it on Kubernetes?
key: There is none: ASF doesn't ship a Helm chart or Kubernetes manifests.
Self-hosting is Docker Compose (docker-compose.self-host.yml via scripts/setup.sh / scripts/asf); the hosted option is Cloud Run (docs/HOSTING.md).
